Uefa will also pay out €5.6m (£4.7m) to teams in the Women's Europa Cup, and a further €6.2m (£5.2m) in 'solidarity payments' to national associations that have at least one club participating in the Champions League. stories.summary: Someone on the Bengals didn't do their homework. Turns out, however, someone on the Bengals didn't do their homework. Since Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles last offseason, the Bengals would actually forfeit a third-round compensatory pick if the trade went through. In other words, the Bengals were about to give up a sixth-round pick and lose a compensatory third-round pick in exchange for Ebiketie, a much steeper cost than the team likely anticipated. After that was pointed out on X by numerous analysts, the trade quickly fell through, with reporters citing that exact issue as the reason the Bengals reneged on the deal.
